title: Australia Tightens Student Transfer Rules: 12-Month Wait Now Required to Switch Providers
excerpt: The temporary change, effective 2 October 2026, doubles the previous six-month restriction and can catch students already studying in Australia — with the clock reset for some.
body:
• From 2 October 2026, most international students in Australia must complete 12 months of their principal course before another provider can enrol them — up from six months.
  • The measure is temporary: the restriction returns to six months on 1 July 2027.
  • Students already studying in Australia can be caught: those who have completed six to twelve months may find the restriction re-applied to them, requiring a release from their current provider.
  • The change is a bridge to bigger mid-2027 migration reforms that will require students to obtain a new visa before transferring providers.

Australia has doubled the waiting period for international students who want to switch education providers, with a temporary 12-month transfer restriction taking effect on 2 October 2026 — and some students already studying in the country could find the clock has been reset.

What changed

The National Code of Practice for Providers of Education and Training to Overseas Students 2018 was amended to temporarily extend the transfer restriction period from six to twelve months for non-school students, until 30 June 2027, according to the Department of Education. From 1 July 2027, the restriction will revert to six months.

The amended Standard 7.1 says that, until 30 June 2027, a registered provider generally cannot knowingly enrol an international student transferring from another registered provider unless the student has completed at least 12 months of their principal course. The amendment was registered on the Federal Register of Legislation on 1 October 2026 and commenced the following day. The six-month restriction for the school sector remains in place.

The catch for students already here

The transitional effect is the most significant practical detail. The Explanatory Statement confirms that students who have completed more than six months but less than 12 months of their principal course when the new rules commence can become subject to the transfer restriction again.

A student who had already passed the previous six-month threshold — and was free to transfer the day before — may now be unable to transfer without a release from their current provider until they have completed 12 months of their principal course. Students who had already completed 12 months before the amendment commenced are unaffected.

Transfers have not been banned. Under the amended Standard 7, a student can still transfer during the restriction period where the releasing provider or the course has ceased to be registered, where the provider has received a sanction preventing the student continuing, where the provider agrees and records the release in PRISMS, or where a government sponsor provides written support. Students can also leave Australia and apply for a new student visa from offshore.

Why the government did it

The government says the temporary extension supports broader migration reforms aimed at strengthening the integrity of the student visa programme. The Explanatory Statement links the change to reforms announced by Immigration Minister Tony Burke on 17 September 2026, expected to introduce a stronger requirement for international students to obtain a new student visa before transferring, taking effect in mid-2027.

From mid-2027, students seeking to change providers after arriving will need to apply through a new Student visa transfer stream, which will prevent transfers to lower-level courses that bypass evidence requirements and disrupt the business models of providers targeting students with low-cost or lower-quality courses after they arrive, according to the Department of Education.

The Explanatory Statement says the extension is intended to mitigate integrity and student welfare risks associated with rushed or non-genuine transfers, including the exploitation of students by unscrupulous receiving providers. The idea is not new: stakeholders advocated a 12-month restriction during the 2022 ESOS Review, and the Senate inquiry into the Education Services for Overseas Students (Quality and Integrity) Bill 2024 heard similar arguments.

What it means for Indian students

Indian students are among the groups most affected: India is one of the largest source markets for Australia's international education sector. Students considering a move should check their provider's transfer and release policies early, since a release recorded in PRISMS is now the main onshore pathway for genuine transfers during the first year.

Providers that primarily recruit international students transferring from other providers may experience a temporary delay in their recruitment pipeline, the government acknowledges.

Part of a wider October package

The transfer change is one of four legislative instruments made law on 2 October 2026. The others restrict onshore Student visa applications and tighten rules on including partners and children in applications. Separately, the Assistant Minister for International Education has specified the BSB80120 Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning) for suspension and cancellation of its CRICOS registration from 5 October 2026, citing significant and systemic integrity issues.

What's next

The 12-month restriction is scheduled to disappear on 1 July 2027 — unless the next round of reforms changes the rules again before then.
